questions.prompt: Which HTML element is the best fit for a page's main navigation links?
questions.explanation: <nav> tells browsers and assistive technology that its contents are navigation, so users can jump straight to it.

questions.prompt: Which CSS declaration makes an element a flex container?
questions.explanation: display: flex turns the element into a flex container so its children can be laid out in a row or column.

questions.prompt: What is the most reliable way to give a text input an accessible name?
choices: Add a <label> linked to the input
questions.explanation: A <label> connected with for/id is announced by screen readers and enlarges the click target. Placeholders disappear and are not a substitute.

questions.prompt: Which Git command records your staged changes as a new snapshot?
questions.explanation: git commit saves what is staged into the repository history. git push only uploads existing commits.

questions.prompt: What is a Git branch?
choices: A movable pointer to a commit that lets work diverge safely
A zipped backup of the project
A copy of the repository stored only on GitHub
questions.explanation: Branches are lightweight pointers to commits, so you can work on a feature without disturbing the main line of work.

questions.prompt: Which keyword declares a variable that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: const prevents reassignment of the binding. (Objects and arrays assigned to a const can still be mutated.)

questions.prompt: How do you run a function when the user clicks a button?
questions.explanation: addEventListener registers a handler for an event type without replacing other handlers on the same element.

questions.prompt: Which array method returns a new array containing only the items that pass a test?
questions.explanation: filter keeps the items for which the callback returns true. map transforms every item, and forEach returns nothing.

questions.prompt: What does await do inside an async function?
choices: Freezes the whole browser until the promise settles
Pauses that function until the promise settles, without blocking the main thread
Runs the following code on a new thread
Turns the promise into a callback
questions.explanation: await suspends only the async function. The event loop keeps running, so the page stays responsive.

questions.prompt: A fetch() request receives an HTTP 404 response. What happens to the promise?
choices: It resolves, so you must check response.ok
questions.explanation: fetch only rejects on network failures. HTTP error statuses still resolve, so check response.ok or response.status.

questions.prompt: How does a parent component pass data to a child component in React?
choices: By editing the child's state directly
By using a global variable called parent
questions.explanation: Props are the inputs to a component. Data flows down from parent to child, and children ask for changes through callback props.

questions.prompt: Why should list items rendered with map() have a stable key?
choices: Keys let React match items between renders so state and DOM nodes are reused correctly
questions.explanation: Without stable keys React can reuse the wrong item when the list is reordered or filtered, causing bugs such as lost input values.

questions.prompt: How do you update state in a function component?
choices: Assign a new value to the variable
Call the setter returned by useState
questions.explanation: Calling the setter schedules a re-render with the new value. Assigning to the variable does not tell React anything changed.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum WCAG AA contrast ratio for normal-size body text?
questions.explanation: WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text and UI components.

questions.prompt: Why use a <button> instead of a clickable <div>?
choices: A button has keyboard support, focus and a role built in
questions.explanation: Native buttons work with Enter and Space, are focusable and are announced as buttons. A div needs all of that rebuilt by hand.

questions.prompt: What should a behavior-focused component test primarily do?
choices: Assert on internal state variable names
Interact like a user and assert on what is visible
questions.explanation: Testing what users see and do keeps tests valid when you refactor the implementation.

questions.prompt: Where should tests run so regressions are caught before code is merged?
choices: Only on a developer's laptop, occasionally
In CI on every pull request
Only when a bug is reported
questions.explanation: Running tests automatically on each pull request gives everyone the same fast feedback before changes reach main.

questions.prompt: Which Core Web Vital measures how quickly the largest visible content element loads?
questions.explanation: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) tracks when the biggest element in the viewport finishes rendering. CLS measures layout shift, and INP measures responsiveness.

questions.prompt: What does Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) measure?
choices: How much visible content unexpectedly moves while the page loads
questions.explanation: CLS captures jumpy layouts, such as images without reserved dimensions pushing text down after it has loaded.

questions.prompt: Which change most directly reduces the cost of oversized images?
choices: Use larger files and shrink them with CSS
questions.explanation: Sending only the pixels the screen needs, in an efficient format, cuts transfer time and speeds up LCP.

questions.prompt: How should a secret API key with write access be handled in a frontend app?
choices: Put it in a client-side environment variable
Never ship it in client code; keep it on a server
questions.explanation: Everything in a client bundle is readable by users, so real secrets must stay on a server that the client calls.

questions.prompt: Why use npm ci instead of npm install in a CI pipeline?
choices: It installs exactly what the lockfile specifies, for reproducible builds
It does not need a package.json
questions.explanation: npm ci installs from package-lock.json and fails if it is out of sync, so CI builds match local builds.
